clue.text: Control break out of one making a bloomer

parts.note: to control something is to master it

indicators.note: the letters of the word break are knocked out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone loses their grip on a break and blunders badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges BREAK into BAKER. A bloomer is a British crusty loaf, so 'making a bloomer' is not making a mistake but baking bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a loaf of bread, and a skilled craftsman who produces such loaves is a master of the bakery trade.

clue.text: Better at one seeing morning over

parts.note: A, the indefinite article, means one
M is a standard abbreviation for morning
when something is over it has come to an end

explanation.surface: Someone finds peace on seeing the night is over and morning has come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is a verb here, meaning to improve; 'at' and 'seeing' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To better a text or law is to improve it, which is just what correcting or revising it does.

clue.text: A slice may be spread round the outside

indicators.note: the outer letters are placed round the farm word, enclosing it
only the outside pair of letters of the word the are used, its first and last letters

parts.note: a spread is American slang for a large farm or ranch

explanation.surface: A slice of toast might have butter spread all round its edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' is not butter but a farm, RANCH; 'the outside' gives T and E, the first and last letters of 'the', which go 'round' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranche is a portion or instalment of something, such as a share issue, much like one cut piece of a larger whole.

clue.text: Agent with song to fix

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A secret agent uses a song to mend something.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend or put right something broken is to fix it.

clue.text: Salts in the drink

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor, and AB (able-bodied seaman) is a sailor, so salts are ABS
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bath salts are dissolved in the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salts' suggests chemistry or bath salts, but in crosswords a salt is a sailor, an AB.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green aniseed-flavoured spirit made with wormwood, a famous alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Relating to the inside of eternal development

indicators.note: a development changes the arrangement, so the letters of eternal are reworked

explanation.surface: A philosophical musing about the inner workings of eternity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' rearranges ETERNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteral is a medical term for things concerning the intestine, the gut within the body.

clue.text: Army angered by award

parts.note: army used as an adjective, as in army life, means military
someone who has been angered is cross

explanation.surface: An army is furious about how a medal has been given out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Military Cross is a British gallantry decoration given to officers for bravery in battle.

clue.text: How morel perhaps shows its maggoty

definitions.text: How morel perhaps shows its maggoty

indicators.note: something maggoty is riddled and disordered, so the letters of how morel are jumbled

explanation.surface: A morel mushroom infested with maggots betrays itself by the holes in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maggoty' rearranges HOW MOREL; the whole clue also describes the answer, since a morel is a mushroom and a grub-eaten one shows burrows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunnel bored by a grub through fruit, wood or a mushroom is a hole made by a worm.

clue.text: Fools one with race of illegal dispatch

parts.note: a fool is an ass, so two fools make two asses in a row
I is the Roman numeral for one
a race or people can be called a nation

explanation.surface: Idiots join an ethnic group in some unlawful scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fools' is plural, so it gives ASS twice, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Murdering a prominent person is an unlawful killing, and to dispatch someone is to kill them.

clue.text: Observe, not without formality

indicators.note: without means the word not is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: to observe something is to notice it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to observe a rule, but without too much stiffness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not without' reads like a double negative, but 'without' removes NOT from NOTICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold, stiff reserve in someone's manner can be called ice, as in breaking the ice.

clue.text: Sites put forward is taking no rejection

parts.note: to posit is to put forward an idea for consideration

indicators.note: is takes the reversed word inside itself

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a rejection throws the word back, so no is read backwards

explanation.surface: Proposed building sites are put forward, and no rejection is taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejection' is read as a refusal, but it is the reversal signal; 'taking' is the container signal, so the turned word goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sites and positions are both places or locations where things are set.

clue.text: Popular enunciation of proclamation

parts.note: something popular is said to be in, fashionable
diction is the clarity of one's enunciation

explanation.surface: A well-loved speaker's clear delivery of a public announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: An indiction was a decree or announcement, historically an imperial edict fixing taxes in Rome.

clue.text: Dance from Burma

indicators.note: the dance is formed from the letters of Burma, rearranged

explanation.surface: A traditional dance originating in Burma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' rearranges BURMA; the dance actually comes from Cuba, not Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a ballroom dance of Cuban origin.

clue.text: One to face Russian maple

indicators.note: to face means to stand in front of, so the card word comes before the abbreviation; the letters also run through face Russian, a coincidence with no hiding signal

parts.note: an ace is a one in a pack of cards
R is a standard abbreviation for Russian; that the answer also runs across face Russian is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A single person must confront a Russian over a maple tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the botanical genus name of the maples.

clue.text: Long legged water carrier

parts.note: suggests a tall wading bird or person fetching water, but means a bridge-like structure on many tall arches that carries water

explanation.definitionFit: An aqueduct is a channel carrying water, often raised across a valley on a row of high arches, its legs.

clue.text: Drunks in the hall know their onions

indicators.note: the hall word is placed in the middle of the drunks word

parts.note: sots are drunkards
taken as written

explanation.surface: The drunkards gathered in the hall are actually experts in their field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'know their onions' is British slang for being expert, but here 'onions' is the definition and 'know their' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Shallots are small mild bulbs of the onion family used in cooking.

clue.text: Poor agronomists not leaving lines on a map

indicators.note: poor signals the letters are in bad shape and rearranged
the letters of the word not are left out of the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: Struggling farm scientists stay put on the contour lines of a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges AGRONOMISTS and 'leaving' takes out N, O and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Isograms are lines joining points of equal value on a map, such as contours or isobars.

clue.text: Yon guest thrown out as most immature

indicators.note: thrown out signals that the letters of yon guest are tossed into disorder

explanation.surface: That visitor over there is ejected for being the most childish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown out' rearranges YON GUEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The youngest of a group is the one with the fewest years and so least mature.

clue.text: Battle with ginger skinned cox not in boat race

indicators.note: only the skin of the word ginger is kept, its first and last letters

parts.note: Cox is a variety of apple, rather than the cox steering a rowing eight in the Oxford-Cambridge Boat Race

explanation.surface: A struggle over a red-haired coxswain who has been left out of the Boat Race crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ginger skinned' leaves G and R, the first and last letters of 'ginger'. The Boat Race is the annual Oxford-Cambridge rowing contest, where a cox steers; here Cox's Orange Pippin, the apple, is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple with a problem or opponent is to struggle or wrestle with it.

clue.text: Incline to implement

definitions.meaning: a slope or tilt, as of a stage
a long-handled garden tool with tines

explanation.definitionFit: A rake is both a slope of a theatre stage or a mast and a toothed tool for gathering leaves.

clue.text: Leave a rock group playing

parts.note: a rock group is a band
something playing is on, as a show is on

explanation.surface: A rock group performing gets out.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon a place or person is to desert them.

clue.text: What pilots are shot out of

definitions.text: What pilots are shot out of

indicators.note: the letters of pilots are shot out and scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A grim question about what aviators are fired from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot out' rearranges PILOTS; the whole clue also defines the weapon from which a shot is fired.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol is a small handgun from which bullets are fired.

clue.text: Concerning aid over trematode

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: over shows the word aid is turned over, read backwards

explanation.surface: A note about aid for a parasitic fluke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns AID into DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A redia is a larval stage of a parasitic flatworm, the trematode or fluke, so the clue gives a broad term for a narrower thing.

clue.text: He may pull strings to get in the band

definitions.text: He may pull strings to get in the band

parts.words: He may pull strings to get in the band
parts.note: suggests someone using influence to join a group, but means a musician plucking the wires of an instrument

explanation.definitionFit: A guitar player plucks its six wires and is a natural member of a rock group.

clue.text: Is having to contend with creepers

indicators.note: the word is has the other word inside it

parts.note: to vie is to contend or compete

explanation.surface: Someone has to struggle with climbing plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is the container signal: one piece holds the other. 'to contend' gives a verb in its bare form.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is a creeping, climbing plant, so plural ivies are creepers.

clue.text: Shan't take in unknown policeman who is a self-seeking toady!

indicators.note: the word shan't takes in, or holds, the other two pieces inside itself

parts.note: shan't loses its apostrophe and is spelt out
Y is a mathematical unknown
a cop is a policeman

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to let in a mystery officer who is a fawning crawler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take in' is the container signal. Y stands for an unknown because algebra labels unknown quantities x, y and z.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant is a flatterer who fawns on the powerful to gain favour.

clue.text: A one party language

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A single-party state's official tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Do is British slang for a party or celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Ido is an artificial international language derived from Esperanto.

clue.text: Set lesbians free from meanness

indicators.note: the letters of set lesbians are set free to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Lesbian women are being liberated from unkindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges SET LESBIANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Beastliness is nastiness or unkindness, behaving horribly, much like meanness.
